unit_bridges.note: FL shows a band's width as a % of the knob; a Q or octave width is put there through this table (the same 0.1-4 octave linear curve as the width controls). Unverified: look at the band's shape in the EQ window (a Q 1.4 bell spans about one octave) and listen.

file_state.evidence: FL 2026 projects with the older 'Fruity Parametric EQ' save 29 little-endian int32s: 7 band levels in 0.01 dB (-200 = -2 dB), 7 frequencies and 7 widths on 0..65536, 7 band types as indices of the options list (defaults 5,6,6,6,6,6,7 = Low shelf, Peaking x5, High shelf). Parametric EQ 2 is assumed to start the same way.
file_state.note: How fl-headless writes Parametric EQ 2 bands straight into a project file (flp_master_tone). NOT verified on a PC for Parametric EQ 2: before any write the layout is proven on FL's own default Parametric EQ 2 preset on this PC (band types must read Low shelf, Peaking x5, High shelf and every level 0 dB); if that fails nothing is written into the file and the bands are set live in FL instead. The int -> value step goes through the controls' curves (int scaled to 0..1 by 'ints'), so a learned map (fl_plugin_map_learn) corrects frequencies/widths too.
